Antiferroelectricity and Antiferroelectric Materials Report

Table of Contents
 1. Abstract
 2. Introduction
 3. Antiferroelectricity
 4. Lead Zirconate
 5. Silver Niobate Tantalate
 6. Hybrid Ferroelectric and Antiferroelectric Materials
 7. Conclusion
 8. References

Abstract

Antiferroelectricity is one of the most actively developing areas in modern physics due to the exceptional parameters of materials with the property. This work aims to review both the phenomenon as a whole and specific substances and their practical utilization. Both the most commonly used materials, such as lead zirconite and their analogs were identified with literature analysis. These include more environmentally friendly elements, such as silver niobate tantalate and promising hybrid compounds. Antiferroelectrics are valuable materials used in the field of energy storage and computer technology, for example, in random access memory.

Introduction

One of the areas of modern science is the discovery and study of the properties and characteristics of various materials. These features can then be applied in a wide variety of fields to obtain better and more reliable items with unique properties. Recently, science has become aware of more particles and processes acting inversely by a well-studied phenomenon. The purpose of the paper is the study of antiferroelectricity, as well as the analysis and review of materials with that property.

Antiferroelectricity

This aspect, as it becomes clear from its name, is the exact opposite of well-studied ferromagnetism. While the latter property is widely found in everyday life, the studied phenomenon is infrequent. However, it is an object of close attention of scientists because of the unique features and capabilities that this state opens. The very essence of it is antiparallel, i.e., towards each other, the arrangement of electric dipole moments in the crystals of certain substances (Electrical4U, 2019). Because of that, instead of the high magnetization of the body, as in ferromagnetism, an extremely low magnetization appears. In an object with similar property, spontaneous polarization is equal to zero since, due to their location, the dipoles in the material cancel each other out.

The reason for the rare spread of the condition is the very unusual conditions for obtaining this phenomenon. Although the requirements vary for each particular material, the principle always remains the same. It is necessary to achieve a specific temperature called the antiferroelectric Curie point to obtain an antiferroelectric phenomenon in a substance, usually a rare-earth metal (Electrical4U, 2019). Otherwise, it is called the Néel point by the scientist who discovered this phenomenon. If the material has a temperature above this value, it loses its unique properties and turns into a paramagnet. Thus, to maintain the antiferroelectric features, it is necessary to sustain the substance’s temperature in a strictly specified range. In this case, the Néel point can be as high as that of lead zirconate PbZrO3, reaching +233 degrees Celsius, or very low, dropping to couples of Kelvin degrees (Electrical4U, 2019). However, the useful attributes of these materials and their potential field of application, which also affects high energy storage devices, make them especially attractive for study.

Lead Zirconate

This material is one of the most famous antiferroelectrics and is widely used in many different areas of human activity. It is used in combination with conventional ferroelectrics and piezoelectric elements, thus expanding the scope of development of non-volatile memory (Burkovsky et al., 2017). The substance is incompletely studied due to its transitions between the magnetic phases. Therefore, the study of lead zirconate continues to this day, even though it has been known as a material for a very long time.

The mixture is a colorless crystalline compound of lead salt and zirconic acid, insoluble in water, and has the chemical formula PbZrO3. In combination with titanium, this compound is widely utilized in piezoelectric elements. In its pure form, lead zirconite is used to create many electronic and radio components, which are crucial to producing high-quality computing and energy technology. Antiferroelectric crystals are used to create various types of actuators, converters, random access memory devices, and even electronic optics (Burkovsky et al., 2017). As mentioned above, lead zirconite is also very promising in the development of energy storage.

A feature of the examination of this material is the incompletely investigated procedure for the transition between magnetic phases. As mentioned above, when forming antiferroelectric materials, the temperature is most often taken into account. Thus, the phase diagram of the dependence of temperature pressure is overestimated, since changes can also occur under the influence of other factors (Burkovsky et al., 2017). Recent studies confirm this since experimentally, two additional phases have been identified that serve as an intermediate between the antiferroelectric and cubic. The presence of new stages that have not yet been thoroughly investigated opens up additional possibilities for experiments on this material and for obtaining properties for use in technology.

Silver Niobate Tantalate

Almost all substances that fall into the category of antiferroelectrics are applied in the energy and high-tech fields. However, there are particular concerns regarding the use of materials containing lead, as previously discussed lead zirconite. Since the utilization of this material is associated with many disputes regarding environmental pollution, alternative solutions that do not include lead are actively being developed (Zhao et al., 2017). These include silver niobite tantalate, by the addition of Ta to AgNbO3, a ferroelectric/antiferroelectric that can be used for similar purposes.

This material is not only more environmentally friendly but also a better alternative to compounds such as Pb(Zr, Ti)O3. When used in the energy storage sector, a silver-based mixture shows better results than lead analogs (Zhao et al., 2017). It is characterized by high-temperature stability since the working range is designated from 20 to 120 degrees Celsius (Zhao et al., 2017). Thus, the compound can be used in a broader range of conditions, which increases the applicability of the material.

Hybrid Ferroelectric and Antiferroelectric Materials

Familiar ferroelectric materials are often contrasted with antiferroelectric due to their nature. In a way, there is competition and disputes between scientists, what kind of condition, and what type of material is more profitable and better suited for specific tasks. However, instead of dividing the elements into two groups according to their phase state, it may be worth trying to combine both sides.

Until recently, this issue was considered exclusively theoretically, without conducting any experiments. In 2018, the first hybrid material Sr3Zr2O7 was introduced, demonstrating a change in polarization at room temperature (Yoshida et al., 2018). This compound is an example of a hybrid proprietary antiferroelectricity that has not previously been encountered in practice. Although the development of this material does not mean its immediate application in practice, the study can be used to develop other types of hybrid substances. Such compounds make it possible to combine the qualities of Ferro- and antiferroelectrics for employment in thermoelectric systems. The property of phase change and competing phases can be used to improve stability.

Conclusion

Thus, antiferroelectricity is currently a rapidly developing field of research due to the many advantages provided by these materials. They can be used both in high-precision technology, random access memory, and energy storage devices. Lead zirconite is currently the most common type of this material. However, soon it can be replaced by more environmentally friendly lead-free analogs and hybrid solutions combining the advantages of Ferro- and antiferroelectrics.

The influence of social media on mental health support in college students is a topic that has gained increasing attention in recent years. With the rise of social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and Snapchat, college students have unprecedented access to information and resources related to mental health. However, the impact of social media on mental health support in college students is complex and multifaceted, with both positive and negative implications.

On one hand, social media provides college students with a platform to connect with others who may be experiencing similar mental health issues. Through online support groups, forums, and communities, students can find a sense of belonging and understanding that may not be readily available in their immediate social circles. Additionally, social media allows for the dissemination of valuable resources and information related to mental health, such as hotlines, counseling services, and self-care tips. This accessibility to support and information can be especially beneficial for college students who may be hesitant to seek help in person due to stigma or other barriers.

However, the influence of social media on mental health support in college students is not without its drawbacks. The curated and idealized nature of social media can contribute to feelings of inadequacy, comparison, and low self-esteem, which are all factors that can negatively impact mental health. The constant exposure to carefully crafted images and narratives of success and happiness can create unrealistic expectations and undermine students' sense of self-worth. Furthermore, the pervasive nature of social media can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, as students may perceive their own experiences as inferior to the seemingly perfect lives of their peers.

Another concerning aspect of social media's influence on mental health support in college students is the potential for misinformation and harmful content. With the abundance of unregulated and unverified information on social media, students may be exposed to inaccurate or harmful advice related to mental health. This can perpetuate myths, stereotypes, and misconceptions about mental illness, leading to further stigmatization and misunderstanding. Additionally, the anonymity and lack of oversight on social media platforms can create an environment where cyberbullying, harassment, and trolling thrive, exacerbating the mental health challenges faced by college students.

In light of these complexities, it is important for college students to critically evaluate the role of social media in their mental health support. While social media can provide valuable connections, resources, and validation, it is essential to approach it with a discerning and self-aware mindset. Students should actively seek out reputable and evidence-based sources of information, cultivate a balanced and diverse social media feed, and be mindful of their own emotional responses to the content they consume.

Moreover, colleges and universities have a responsibility to address the influence of social media on mental health support in their student populations. By implementing education and awareness programs, promoting mental health resources, and fostering a culture of open dialogue and support, institutions can mitigate the negative impact of social media while harnessing its potential for positive change. Additionally, mental health professionals and counselors should be attuned to the unique challenges and pressures that social media poses for college students, and incorporate this awareness into their support and interventions.

In conclusion, the influence of social media on mental health support in college students is a complex and nuanced issue. While social media has the capacity to connect students with support, resources, and understanding, it also poses risks related to comparison, misinformation, and harmful content. As college students navigate the digital landscape, it is crucial for them to approach social media mindfully and critically, while institutions and mental health professionals must also adapt to the evolving challenges and opportunities presented by social media. Ultimately, by fostering a healthy and informed relationship with social media, college students can harness its potential to support and enhance their mental well-being.

In Herman Melville's epic novel, Moby Dick, the character of Captain Ahab is one of the most complex and enigmatic figures in literature. Ahab is a man consumed by a singular, obsessive quest for vengeance against the elusive white whale, Moby Dick. Throughout the novel, Ahab's character is portrayed as larger than life, possessed by an almost fanatical determination to hunt down and destroy the object of his obsession. His relentless pursuit of the whale serves as a metaphor for the destructive and all-consuming nature of man's primal urges and the consequences of unchecked ambition.

Ahab is depicted as a commanding and charismatic leader, possessing an almost hypnotic power over his crew. He is a figure of authority and reverence, with a commanding presence that demands respect and obedience from those around him. His leadership style is both inspiring and tyrannical, as he drives his crew to the brink of madness in pursuit of his own personal vendetta against Moby Dick.

Despite his commanding presence, Ahab is also a deeply troubled and tormented individual. His obsession with revenge has consumed him to the point of madness, and he is driven by a deep sense of existential despair. His monomaniacal pursuit of the whale is a desperate attempt to assert his dominance over the forces of nature and fate that have conspired against him. Ahab's obsession with Moby Dick serves as a reflection of his own inner turmoil and the struggle to find meaning and purpose in a world that seems indifferent to his suffering.

Ahab's character is also defined by his complex relationship with the natural world. He is a man at war with the elements, driven by a fierce determination to conquer the untamed forces of the sea. His quest for vengeance against Moby Dick is, in many ways, a battle against the primal and uncontrollable forces of nature that threaten to overwhelm him. Ahab's obsession with the whale represents his futile attempt to impose order and control over the chaotic and unpredictable world in which he lives.

In addition to his internal struggles, Ahab is also a figure of tragic hubris. His relentless pursuit of the whale is driven by a sense of pride and arrogance, as he believes himself to be invincible in the face of the natural world. His hubris blinds him to the consequences of his actions and leads to the destruction of both himself and those around him. Ahab's tragic flaw is his inability to recognize the limits of his own power and the futility of his quest for revenge.

Ahab's character is further complicated by his moral ambiguity. While he is driven by a sense of righteous indignation and a desire for justice, his pursuit of the whale leads him to commit acts of cruelty and inhumanity. He is willing to sacrifice the lives of his crew and forsake all moral and ethical considerations in his quest for vengeance. Ahab's moral descent mirrors his descent into madness, as he becomes increasingly consumed by his obsession with the whale.

Ultimately, Captain Ahab is a character defined by his relentless pursuit of vengeance and his tragic inability to escape the consequences of his own actions. His obsession with Moby Dick is a reflection of his own inner turmoil and existential despair, as he grapples with the forces of nature and fate that threaten to overwhelm him. Ahab's character serves as a cautionary tale about the destructive power of unchecked ambition and the consequences of succumbing to the darker impulses of the human spirit.

The Role of Propaganda in Twentieth-Century Conflicts

Throughout the twentieth century, propaganda played a significant role in shaping public opinion and influencing the outcomes of various conflicts. Propaganda, defined as the dissemination of biased or misleading information to promote a particular political ideology or agenda, was employed by both governments and non-state actors to rally support, demonize enemies, and manipulate public perception. This paper aims to explore the multifaceted role of propaganda in twentieth-century conflicts, examining its methods, impact, and ethical implications.

One of the earliest examples of propaganda in the twentieth century can be traced back to World War I. Governments on all sides of the conflict utilized propaganda as a means to mobilize their populations and maintain morale. In the United States, for instance, the Committee on Public Information (CPI) was established to shape public opinion in favor of the war effort. The CPI employed various techniques, such as posters, pamphlets, and films, to depict the enemy as barbaric and promote patriotism among citizens. These efforts aimed to create a sense of unity and justify the sacrifices made by the population.

Similarly, Nazi Germany under Adolf Hitler extensively used propaganda during World War II to manipulate public sentiment and promote their fascist agenda. The Nazi regime controlled all media outlets, ensuring that only information that aligned with their ideology was disseminated. Propaganda films, such as Leni Riefenstahl's "Triumph of the Will," glorified Hitler and the Nazi Party, presenting them as saviors of the German nation. The effectiveness of Nazi propaganda is evident in the widespread support garnered by Hitler and the compliance of the German population in the implementation of discriminatory policies and the Holocaust.

The role of propaganda extended beyond state actors in the twentieth century, with non-state actors also employing these techniques to further their goals. One notable example is the use of propaganda by revolutionary movements during the Cold War. Communist organizations, such as the Chinese Communist Party and the Cuban Revolution led by Fidel Castro, utilized propaganda to gain support and legitimize their ideologies. Posters, speeches, and publications were crafted to depict the ruling regimes as oppressive and the revolutionaries as liberators. This propaganda not only aimed to rally domestic support but also sought to inspire international solidarity among like-minded movements.

Propaganda also played a crucial role in the context of the Vietnam War. The United States government, through the creation of the Vietnam Information Bureau, disseminated propaganda to shape public opinion in favor of the war. The bureau produced films and news articles that portrayed the war as a necessary fight against communism and framed the Vietnamese people as grateful recipients of American intervention. However, the effectiveness of this propaganda was undermined by an increasingly skeptical public, as the horrors of war were broadcasted on television screens, challenging the official narrative.

The impact of propaganda extended beyond the immediate conflict, shaping long-term perceptions and historical memory. For example, the Soviet Union utilized propaganda to rewrite history and create a heroic narrative of the Great Patriotic War, as they called World War II. Soviet propaganda depicted the Soviet people as the sole saviors of Europe, downplaying the contributions of other Allied forces. This narrative continued to shape historical accounts and public memory long after the conflict ended, reinforcing the Soviet Union's self-perception as a mighty superpower.

Ethically, the use of propaganda raises questions about the manipulation of truth and the limits of information control. Propaganda often distorts facts, exaggerates threats, and dehumanizes the enemy. By appealing to emotions rather than rationality, it can exploit people's fears and prejudices, leading to the justification of violence and discrimination. Moreover, the monopolization of information by governments or powerful entities undermines the principles of democracy and free speech, limiting the ability of individuals to make informed decisions.

In conclusion, propaganda played a significant role in shaping the outcomes of conflicts in the twentieth century. Governments and non-state actors alike utilized various techniques to manipulate public opinion, rally support, and demonize enemies. From World War I to the Cold War and beyond, propaganda was a powerful tool that influenced historical memory and shaped the perceptions of nations. However, the ethical implications of propaganda cannot be ignored, as it often distorts truth and manipulates emotions. As we move forward, it is crucial to remain vigilant and critical of the information we consume, ensuring that propaganda does not undermine the principles of democracy and human rights.

Hotel Industry: Choosing the Right Location Report (Assessment)

Several factors are put into consideration before any business enterprise or entity is established. Among them is the physical location. Hotel industry, like any other business activity has to put this factor ahead of all other factors if indeed any tangible gains are to be realized out of the business. The place where a hotel is located will determine several other things including sales volume, customers, profitability and long-term survival in the industry.

It is evident that a convenient place to up a hotel should consider factors such as commercial areas, recreational grounds, airports among others .These factors can maintain good customer base as well as attracting more new customers. There has been always a controiversy on whether it’s more beneficial to put up a hotel where there are other similar hotels or away from such businesses.

One theory argues that by creating a business venture close to the competitors geographically, an entrepreneur can obtain posive externality from economic and institutional environments. In contrast, it is disputed that by locating business venture far away from its competitors, the firm will avoid localized competition and earns itself competitive advantage. Because the two theories seem to be o great importance, it’s good to consider the two in some aspects while putting up a hotel business.

In most cases, it’s rare to establish a business without competitors, in other words almost all business entities operate under perfect competition characterized by product homogeneity, many sellers and buyers and above all buyers and sellers are price takers. Therefore it is important that while opening a new hotel location, one should bear in mind that there are other existing similar businesses and one should not make decisions that to some extend will affect the operations of other investors.

One aspect which can clearly indicate he interruptions of other firms operations is the product priced in other competitors which include pricing of various goods and services including market’ local room rates offerd by the hoteliers. Therefore, one should come up with sound decisions which will not negatively influence the existing market’s room rates (Magnini & Honeycutt, 2003).

The world has become a global village and the survival for the fittest is the ultimate goal for every investor. Because of the competitive nature of the hotel industry, every one involved in the business strives very hard to get his/her own share in the market place.

For this reason, it’s very easy for one to resort into unfair practices such as making the prices of your products lower than those of your competitors. The prices of commodities should directly proportional to the Quantity and the quality of goods and services offered, therefore, once a new hotel is established it to avoid unfair competition, it should offer almost similar services at the same prices with the other competitors.

Alternatively an entrepreneur might opt to provide better and superior services than the existing competitor at the existing market rate. As a manager of a hotel, one should be able to determine critically the value and price of a hotel location in setting room rates (Bull, 1994).

As pointed out later, the pricing of rooms in a hotel is dependent on several factors. For instance several studies have found out that hotels located in the3 cities or near some facilities like airports tend to be expensive than those located away from such prices. An entrepreneur might be operating two hotel facilities offering similar services under different geographical regions but the pricing of the rooms is not the same. This is due to prevailing conditions and environments under which these two entities operate.

It is therefore important to conform to the existing practices oaf the other hotel operators so as to avoid rivalry in the business. However in the process of ensuring that one does not influence the market’s local room rate, profit maximization goal should be fulfilled through ensuring that a firm does not underpriced its products otherwise losses would be incurred and even the firm will be kicked out of the business at its initial stages of operations(Cho, 2003).

Most important is that quality rather than quantity is more valued in hotel industry, so when pricing the rooms they should be priced according to their quality and this will help maintain harmonious working environment among other different players in the industry.

Any customer in need of a certain good or service would want to get it more conveniently and at a very convenient place. The two most important goals to fulfill while running up a business are profit maximization and customer satisfaction.

However, the former is dependent on the latter since no income generation without first satisfying the customers. So the most important issue to consider while putting up a new hotel is where the customers would find it more appropriate to enjoy their services. While putting up high-rise hotels in city areas, it is imperative to bear in mind the problems which come across with this decision to the local population and the tourist such as huge traffic congestion and escalating pollution.

In most cases, the burden for improving and dealing with these problems is left in the hands of tax-payers. While pursuing the principle of self interest I business ventures, public interest should be taken care of so as not to make profits at the expense of harming the general public(Shoval & Cohen-Hattab,2001).

The other important feature to consider while selecting location for a hotel is the demographic characteristics of the target population. Different groups of people have different needs. For instance, there is no logic to open up a Chinese restaurant in a place where the people available don’t consume Chinese foods.

Besides, there are some people with their own taboos and customs which prohibit them from consuming certain foods like in the case of Muslims who don’t consume pork, therefore you should not locate a hotel in a Muslim invaded community if at all you know your hotel businesses offer pork related products (Bull, 1994).

Another important issue to put in consideration while selecting a new location for hotel development is the social and economic class of the surrounding population (Chou, Hsu & Chen, 2008). A five-star hotel cannot be situated in a rural set up consisting of primitive dwellers or small towns with low income earners and whose integrity and ability to spend in such hotels a re questionable. The services and facilities offered should match the social class of the people being targeted (Yoon, Chen & Gursoy, 1999).

Security is another critical issue that cannot be ignored while setting up a hotel. Public order issues including the possibility of fire outbreak, theft and robbery can influence the customer base in a given physical location. Hotels are not only national but international facilities which attract customers across the entire globe.

It should be noted that provision of hotel services is one component of tourism for a given country and tourism income constitute a significant percentage of country’s Gross Domestic Product. All the major international hotel facilities should be located in safe and secure places so as to attract foreign tourists and customers.

This area should be terror-free zones and that explains the reasons why the tourism industry in peaceful countries keeps on growing at a very high rate. The reasons attributed to this are two, one so many investors are willing to venture their businesses in these nations and two too many foreigners are attracted to these nations (Cox & Vieth, 2003).

Running a successful hotel industry is a big challenge. That is why brilliant managers with high thinking and reasoning capacity coupled with critical thinking are recommended to run these businesses. And this is where the strategic management comes in. as a manager I my local area if I were to run a hotel, the first thing is to do through marketing research to establish very well the nature of the groups of people around the area(Liu & Var,1986).

But before going into that, looking at glance, majority of the people are local community groups majority being low-income earners and afe medium income earners. There are no complex needs required to be formulated to satisfy these people therefore few things would only require to be implemented. In such an area like this, a huge percentage of the people do perform odd jobs, others are jobless and few have got formal jobs (Urtasun, 2006; Lindberg & Johnson, 1997).

In addition a better pricing methodology will need to be adopted so as to make the accommodation more affordable.

The nature of services provided will be very much determined by the kind of staffing and human resources available. Local people can be well pleased when served by the people they know better, therefore employing local people will retain huge customer base to some extend. In such situations there is no need for complex staffing as some customers might need to be approached using local language they can easily understand.

An important thing to note about these groups people is that they are of different ethnic groups and you cannot identify a particular community of group to be your customer. Therefore the services should vary accordingly so as t accommodate each and everyone in the given area. This will vary in form of foods, drinks offered as well as the entertainment (Johnson & Vanetti, 2005; Chen, 2001).

Management of a hotel in an isolated area requires a different approach from managing a hotel in a place where other hotels are located. This is because such a facility will not enjoy the benefits of positive externalities enjoyed by the one located in the city or central business district of a given nation.

High quality service delivery should be given the first priority since there are no other similar surrounding facilities (Brougham & Butler, 1981). There has always been a principle of differentiation which emphasizes on the concept of cluster concept which is as a result of behavior of consumers asking for quotations. In the process of minimizing the transportation costs incurred when the consumers are seeking market information, several hotels will always engage in cluster concept (Bachleitner & Zins, 1999).

A newly established hotel in an isolated area cannot enjoy all these benefits and therefore as a manager Ione should formulate and implement decisions on how to access the consumers and provide them with relevant information. The first strategies should be geared towards making the customers aware of the products available and win their confidence.

This might involve massive expensive advertising which need to be an international one since the hotel is interested in both domestic and international customers. In the event that the hotel in isolation is in a place with limited support facilities such as banks supermarkets, a manager can make steps to liase with the concerned managers or directors of these facilities to initiate the bringing up of the same. This is because they play a very crucial role as far as attracting the customers is concerned (Andriotis, 2005).

The efficient running, smooth control and coordination of operations in an hotel as well as maintaining experienced staff and human resource management team is a very crucial requirement to ensure the existence and also deal with challenges associated with increasing competition.

The manager should apply the principle of professionalism and all the departments should be headed by the experienced professionals (Teye, Sonmez & Sirakaya, 2002). The emergence of a new hotel into the market may lead to several outcomes such as new guests moving into the newly established property and leaving other properties and decline in rates offered by the other competitors as a result of new entrance into the market(Egan, Knowles, & Bey,2000).

Launching of training programmers for the employees both existing ones and the already existing work in hotel industry has been widely used in order to improve service delivery and help the new hotel compete fairly in the global market. This helps in bringing up competent staff hence ensuring superior services.

Delegation of duties, right a correct channels of communications are some of the other principles that should be observed while managing the resources of an organization. Management decisions will determine the firm’s future and in the event that such decisions are not well made the firm might very easily be eliminated from the market. Also as a manager you should be able to predict what the proportion of foreign customers might be (Weaver & Lawton, 2001).

Stress Management Report

Table of Contents
 1. Introduction
 2. Causes of Stress at Work
 3. Stress Management
 4. Conclusion
 5. List of References

Introduction

Stress Management has been an issue to various managements in both public and private sectors. Productivity and efficiency are directly affected by the ability of employees to manage their stress in an effective manner. The management should therefore help them reduce their level of stress through these methods: institutional programs, collateral programs, training and development, and support incentives. If stress is managed properly, organizations can reduce costs that arise due to employees stress.

Causes of Stress at Work

Many organizations in the world, both in public and private sectors, are facing many challenges that range from economic recession, international insecurity, increasingly knowledgeable customers and cutthroat competition in the market. Business environment has become unfriendly, and survival of firms largely depends on how best the management can approach the current market changes. Daft (2010, p.432) explains that for a firm to be effective in its operations, there must be emphasis on the human aspect.

The employees must be put at the forefront and they must understand the strategic objectives of the institution. Employees are also faced with many issues such as job insecurity, poor working conditions, family issues and career ambition among others that affect their performance.

Stress among employees poses a serious threat to development of any organization. World Health Organization, in its recent reports, has stated that stress is a major cause of many health problems. Stress also reduces the attention of an individual to less than 50%(Lake, Griffiths and Cox, 2003, p.5). Stress has made many employees lose their lives at workplaces, especially those dealing with heavy and dangerous plants.

A driver can easily lose focus of the road if s/he is under an uncontrolled level of stress. This can lead to loss of not just his/her life, but also those of other important employees.Upon this basis, this report was conducted in order to come up with ways through which stress can be put in control. From the findings of the report, I came to improve my knowledge on the causes, Implications and ways of managing stress.

While undertaking the survey on management of stress in organizations, I came to realize that the sources of stress to employees are many and vary from one employee to another.

While some employees are stressed by lack of ambition to improve their careers, others are affected by the poor working conditions and low wages. In addition, family issues at home affect the performances of other employees. Lastly, employees are stressed by work related stress such as the type of job performed or the supervision and management received in the course of duty.

In order to manage stress, it is important that an organization and its employees identify the causes of stress. I realized that it is in the light of these causes of stress that stress can be effectively managed at work. This is because the programs set up to manage stress are focused on eliminating the cause of stress and alleviating the effects to both the individual employee and the firm

Stress Management

While conducting survey on stress management in organizations, I realized that many scholars have conducted research on issues related to stress. The scholars have examined how it affects the output and the general success of firms. Their findings converge at the point that stress leads to serious failures and if not taken care of in time, an organization can be forced to fold up its operation.

Competition in the current market is so stiff that a little dissatisfaction from a customer will lead to his avoidance from it in his next visit. While employees serve the firm’s customers, they too manufacture the products. Any dissatisfaction on their part could be detrimental to the performance of the firm.

I came across Parker (2007, p.23) who asserts that organizations should have proper stress management units to avoid situations where employees transfer their stress to customers; through poor customer service. Leka, Griffiths and Cox (2003, p. 3) taught me that work related stress are because of mismatching of work assignment and employees abilities.

An employee is given a task that is out of his/her scope. They hence strain to attain the requirements of the task, leading to stress. Management should make an effort and match employee’s capabilities and their skills.

In spite of the urgent need to manage stress, I learnt that stress management could be complex. Fried (2008, p. 61) posits that stress management units within a firm can use various techniques to reduce strains among the employees.Form these authors, I leant that some of the organizations I surveyed have employed various stress management techniques some of which include these.

In the course of my survey, I learnt that many firms have employed collateral programs, which I came to realize encourage employees to move on with life. Through these programs, employees are able to manage their stress while improving their performance. Some of the collateral programs I came across included the health promotion programs, employee wellness programs and stress management programs.

Such programs contain many activities that improve the activities of an organization with regard to the needs of an employee. An important lesson is that the wellness of employees is not only about the physical health of employees but about the surrounding environment and things that affect the employees both directly and indirectly (Cunningham 2000, p. 109).

I found out that some organizations employed institutional programs to reduce the stress among their employees. Such institutional programs entailed various mechanisms employing many strategies to reduce stress. For instance, I found one organization using the work balance strategy that aimed at establishing a balance between work and social life. This strategy entailed redesigning various jobs for employees such as working in shifts rather than over time.

In order to reduce and contain stress on organizations, I found out that other firms have incorporated other stress management programs. For instance, one firm had begun training and development program for its employees as well as technical skills training programs. Through such programs, I learnt that the firm wanted to reduce stress related to type of job an employee does.

In addition, while other firms were intervening by training their employees on ways of managing stress, other employers had established support intervention centers in the firm.

Under such centers, any employee perceived of being stressed by any issue either at work or at home would visit such centers. According to the findings of my survey, the centers had proved an effective way of managing stress in organizations since organizations reported reduced stress among their employees and improved performance (Weinberg, Southerland & Cooper, 2010, p. 61).

Conclusion

Stress at workplace is a factor that managements cannot afford to overlook currently. Its effects are devastating and it can completely paralyze the normal operation of a firm. For this reason, many organizations have come up with various means of managing stress. Some of the methods put forward are institutional programs, collateral programs, training and development, technical skills and support incentives. All these programs work towards achieving a stress free working environment.

The art of calligraphy has been practiced across different cultures for centuries, and it remains an essential part of human expression. Calligraphy is the art of beautiful writing, and it involves the use of various writing tools such as pens, ink, and brushes to create visually pleasing and artistic text. Different cultures have developed their unique styles and techniques of calligraphy, which reflect their history, beliefs, and values. In this essay, we will explore the different forms of calligraphy across cultures, their history, and their significance in human expression.

Calligraphy in China is known as "shufa," and it dates back to the Han Dynasty (202 BC-220 AD). The art of calligraphy was highly valued in ancient China, and it was considered an essential skill for scholars and officials. The most famous form of Chinese calligraphy is "cursive script," which is a flowing and elegant style that emphasizes the beauty of the lines. Another popular form of calligraphy in China is "seal script," which is characterized by its bold and strong strokes. Chinese calligraphy has also influenced other Asian countries such as Japan and Korea, where it is known as "shodou" and "hangeul," respectively.

In Japan, calligraphy is known as "shodou" and has been practiced for over 1,000 years. Japanese calligraphy is characterized by its simplicity, elegance, and flexibility. The most popular form of Japanese calligraphy is "kaisho," which is a straightforward and simplistic style that emphasizes clarity and legibility. Another popular form of Japanese calligraphy is "sousho," which is a more ornate and decorative style that is often used for decorative purposes. Japanese calligraphy has also influenced other art forms such as painting, sculpture, and architecture.

In the Middle East, calligraphy is known as "khatt," and it has been practiced for over 1,400 years. Arabic calligraphy is characterized by its elaborate and ornate style, which is often used for religious and cultural purposes. The most famous form of Arabic calligraphy is "thuluth," which is a highly decorative style that emphasizes the beauty of the letters. Another popular form of Arabic calligraphy is "naskh," which is a more simplistic and legible style that is often used for everyday writing. Arabic calligraphy has also influenced other art forms such as pottery, textiles, and architecture.

In the West, calligraphy has been practiced for over 2,000 years, and it has played an essential role in the development of Western art and culture. In ancient Rome and Greece, calligraphy was used for official documents, and it was considered an essential skill for scholars and officials. During the Middle Ages, calligraphy was used for religious purposes, and it was often used to decorate manuscripts and illuminations. In the Renaissance, calligraphy was revived as an essential part of humanist education, and it was used to create beautiful and artistic texts. In modern times, calligraphy has been used for a variety of purposes, including advertising, packaging, and graphic design.

In conclusion, calligraphy is an essential part of human expression across cultures. It reflects the history, beliefs, and values of different cultures, and it has played an essential role in the development of art and culture. Calligraphy is an art form that requires skill, creativity, and patience, and it continues to inspire and captivate people around the world. Whether it is used for official documents, religious purposes, or artistic expression, calligraphy remains an essential part of human expression across cultures.

The Founding Fathers of America Essay

Table of Contents
 1. Introduction
 2. The Founding Father’s Notion
 3. Defending this Notion
 4. Legal Plunder
 5. References

Introduction

America’s founding fathers advocated and acted upon division of powers. They did this because they knew if all the powers were left to the federal government; it was likely that it would impose unnecessary limitations to individuals thus interfering with their liberty. Therefore, they advocated for a system in which the power of the federal government would be divided among three different branches, which were: the executive, legislative and judiciary. This was a horizontal division and distribution of powers so that each of these could become a watchdog to the other. The term Founding Fathers refers to a group of revolutionary people who were united in finding a peaceful and united America, even though they represented different professions. They all fought for American Liberty and this had put a great significance to date. This is because the foundation that they laid has provided a strong ground where today’s America has been built (Matzke, 2009. Pp.0-89).

The Founding Father’s Notion

According to Frank, 2006, America’s founding fathers believed that any successful government has to derive its legitimate powers from the people it is governing. They upheld the fact that all people were created equal and that they need to be given an opportunity to exercise rights that could not be taken away from them. They referred to these rights as unalienable and they included rights to life, rights to liberty and rights to pursue happiness. Any government has a duty to protect these rights and whenever it derails from this path, the citizens have a right to abolish it and to institute a new one that will govern with these rights in its mind. This brought about revolution and a radical shift in politics. The founding fathers advocated that the government should not impose rights upon people rather these people should give the government limited powers in its governing (Frank 2006).

Defending this Notion

Overtime, this notion can be proved to be true in the entire America. This is because, it would be a great shock to these founding fathers if they woke up and found the land that they fought for has become different. They believed that America was going to be a land of opportunity and freedom if there was minimal government intrusion into the liberty of individuals. They also believed that there should be a limited central government created to protect people and provide safe environment for them to pursue happiness. The government has interfered with the rights of the citizens and they are no longer able to live in liberty as the founding fathers wished. According to Matzke, 2009, government is trading the liberty of individuals in the name of security; there is no longer defined role of government as it were in the days of the founding fathers. The government of America has continued to expand and this has led to the contraction of the rights of individuals.

Frank, 2006 argues that the founding fathers insisted on the supremacy of individual rights when they were drafting the constitution. The document advocates that citizens should be allowed to enjoy the work of their hands. They advocated that a sovereign federal government would be weak if it did not derive its powers from the citizens but rather from a small group of people in power. The notion of these founding fathers has been proved to be true to date since the government started imposing powers on its citizens rather than upholding what the citizens advocate for. The federal government has given itself more powers than advocated by the founding fathers and this has affected all industries because they are all governed by federal powers The growth of the population has also led to a farfetched relationship between the citizens and their representatives. The only solution would be for the federal government to go back to the rules of the founding fathers that advocated liberty so that individuals were free to move to any part of America where they feel that they are well represented (Frank 2006).

Legal Plunder

This involves the laws set aside to safeguard individual liberties, freedoms and rights necessary for survival. It emphasizes on what is individually owned in a legitimate way and should not be alienated from them whatsoever. The founding fathers had this notion in mind where they advocated for respect of all American citizens however the federal government has violated this identity for the citizens in some circumstance by the name of fight against crime and terrorism. In close examination of this notion, founding fathers desired that no individual should posses something at the expense of the other using illegal means like staling. However the American society has experienced a drastic transformation in the social and economic set ups created by predominant capitalism practiced in America (Frank 2006).

Capitalism has created social classes contrary to wishes of our founding fathers which advocated for a just society. This has as well witnessed increased rates of crime and other social evils in the society. The government has also contributed to this menace through imposition of certain laws and regulations which victimize and disadvantage some Americans resulting to crimes and unjust society (Matzke, 2009).

Artistic expression serves as the lifeblood of cultural identity, a relationship as intricate and colorful as the patterns woven into the fabric of a traditional garment. This connection between art and cultural identity is an eternal dance, choreographed by the human experience and performed across the canvas of time. To understand the depth of this relationship, one must first delve into the concept of cultural identity itself. Cultural identity is the sense of belonging to a group which shares common characteristics such as language, traditions, values, behaviors, and artifacts. It is an anchor, providing a sense of place and purpose in the vast sea of humanity. Art, in its myriad forms--be it painting, music, literature, dance, or sculpture--acts as the most eloquent and profound expression of this identity, crystallizing the intangible essence of a culture into tangible forms.

Art and cultural identity are often so deeply intertwined that one serves as a mirror to the other. Just as a mirror reflects the visage of a person, so does art reflect the collective soul of a culture. In many societies, traditional art is not simply a matter of aesthetics but is imbued with spiritual, historical, and communal significance. For instance, the Aboriginal Dreamtime paintings of Australia are not merely eye-catching designs; they are storied maps, offering insights into the spiritual beliefs and ancestral tales of the artists’ indigenous communities. Through these vibrant expressions, the Aboriginal culture communicates its deep connection with the land and the Dreamtime, the sacred era of creation according to their mythology.

Similarly, cultural identity manifests itself in the rhythmic beats of African drums, which are far more than musical instruments. They are historical chronicles and mediums of communication, echoing the tales and messages of a people across the savannah. In West African societies, the Djembe drum is not just an object to produce sound but a sacred item that captures the pulse of the community, its rituals, and celebrations. It is through music and dance that the cultural identity of these communities is celebrated, preserved, and transmitted from one generation to the next. The rhythms and movements are a language of their own, speaking of ancestry, unity, and the human spirit's indomitable joy.

The relationship between artistic expression and cultural identity can also be observed in literature, where the written word serves as a repository for the collective memory and values of a culture. Literary works often provide a voice to the voiceless, a narrative to the marginalized, and a platform for cultural introspection and discourse. The impact of colonialism on indigenous health has been a profound and enduring one, with far-reaching consequences that continue to be felt to this day. The arrival of European colonizers in various parts of the world brought about significant changes in the lives of indigenous populations, including their health and well-being. The imposition of new systems of governance, economic exploitation, and cultural assimilation had a detrimental effect on the health of indigenous communities, leading to widespread suffering and the loss of traditional knowledge and practices related to health and healing.

One of the most significant impacts of colonialism on indigenous health was the introduction of new diseases to which indigenous populations had little to no immunity. The arrival of European explorers and settlers in the Americas, Africa, Asia, and the Pacific brought with it a host of infectious diseases such as smallpox, measles, influenza, and tuberculosis, which decimated indigenous populations. The lack of immunity to these diseases, combined with the often unsanitary living conditions imposed by colonial authorities, led to devastating epidemics that wiped out entire communities and significantly reduced the overall population of indigenous peoples.

In addition to the direct impact of new diseases, colonialism also had indirect effects on indigenous health through the disruption of traditional lifestyles and the imposition of new social and economic structures. The forced displacement of indigenous peoples from their ancestral lands, the destruction of traditional food sources and hunting grounds, and the introduction of new dietary habits and lifestyles all contributed to a decline in the overall health and well-being of indigenous communities. The loss of access to traditional healing practices and the imposition of Western medical systems further compounded the health challenges faced by indigenous peoples.

Furthermore, the colonial project often led to the marginalization and disempowerment of indigenous communities, which in turn had a negative impact on their health. The imposition of new legal and political systems, the dispossession of land and resources, and the suppression of indigenous cultural practices and languages all contributed to a sense of social and cultural dislocation among indigenous peoples, leading to high rates of substance abuse, mental health issues, and other forms of social and psychological distress. The loss of self-determination and autonomy over their own lives and health has had lasting consequences for indigenous communities, contributing to ongoing health disparities and inequities.

The legacy of colonialism continues to shape the health outcomes of indigenous populations around the world. The intergenerational trauma resulting from centuries of oppression, dispossession, and cultural genocide has had a profound impact on the mental, emotional, and physical health of indigenous communities. The ongoing effects of colonialism, including poverty, lack of access to quality healthcare, and environmental degradation, continue to contribute to higher rates of chronic diseases, infant mortality, and other health disparities among indigenous peoples.

In recent years, there has been growing recognition of the need to address the historical and ongoing impacts of colonialism on indigenous health. Efforts to decolonize healthcare systems, promote culturally sensitive and responsive care, and support indigenous-led initiatives for health and healing are important steps towards addressing the health disparities faced by indigenous communities. These efforts must be accompanied by broader social and political changes to address the root causes of health inequities, including the recognition of indigenous rights to self-determination, land, and resources, and the promotion of indigenous knowledge and practices related to health and healing.

In conclusion, the impact of colonialism on indigenous health has been profound and enduring, with far-reaching consequences that continue to be felt to this day. The introduction of new diseases, the disruption of traditional lifestyles, and the marginalization of indigenous communities have all contributed to the health disparities faced by indigenous populations around the world. Efforts to address these disparities must take into account the historical and ongoing impacts of colonialism and work towards promoting indigenous self-determination, cultural revitalization, and access to quality, culturally sensitive healthcare. Only through a comprehensive and holistic approach can the health and well-being of indigenous peoples be truly addressed and improved.

Greetings, my dear reader! Today, I'm going to write an essay about something that is quite dear to my heart: the importance of belly laughs. You see, in our fast-paced world filled with stress, worries, and constant demands, it's easy to forget the simple joys in life. And one of those joys, in my humble opinion, is the ability to laugh until your belly hurts. So, put on your comfiest pajamas, grab a warm cup of cocoa, and get comfortable because we're about to embark on an adventure of exploring the wonderful world of laughter!

Before we dive in, let's define what exactly a belly laugh is. A belly laugh is that contagious, uncontrollable burst of laughter that comes from deep within your abdomen. It's the kind of laughter that makes your stomach muscles ache, your eyes water, and your cheeks hurt from smiling so much. It's a genuine expression of joy and happiness that is unique to human beings. And believe it or not, it has numerous benefits for both our physical and mental health.

First and foremost, laughing releases endorphins in our brains. Endorphins are natural painkillers and mood elevators that help reduce stress

Luther and his colleagues introduced the new order of worship during their visitation of the Electorate of Saxony, which began in 1527. They also assessed the standard of pastoral care and Christian education in the local parishes. In Wittenberg, Luther had been giving his sermons in German since 1517. From the beginning of the Reformation, he regarded the preaching of the gospel in the vernacular as a key element of his religious reforms. He was determined to change the preaching and worship in the churches. His goal was to make the Bible accessible to all and to ensure that the gospel was preached and taught everywhere. Catechisms and hymnals were produced in the vernacular, and schooling was improved, so that children and adults were able to read the Bible and sing hymns. Luther himself composed a German Mass, published in 1526, which was to be used in all the churches in the Electorate of Saxony. This was a short but complete service, with no room for additions or changes by the priests. In the service, the congregation took an active part: they recited the words of institution (This is my body... this is my blood...), and the "Agnus Dei" (Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world...). The musical setting of the Mass remained in Latin until 1545, when Luther published a German version. It was the first vernacular Mass to be printed with musical notation. He wrote a new melody for the Agnus Dei and suggested that it could be sung as a chorale, that is, with everyone joining in. Luther also composed a German liturgy for private devotions in the home, to be said at mealtimes, and for other special occasions such as weddings and funerals. These services were very similar to the church services, and in this way Luther sought to unify public and private devotions. He also wanted to replace the old superstitious beliefs and practices with Christian teaching and to ensure that the gospel was at the heart of people's everyday lives. Luther's early efforts to introduce a vernacular liturgy provoked strong opposition, even among some of his supporters. In Saxony, the early services were recited rather than sung, and the congregation took an active part. Luther insisted that music should play a greater role in the services. He drew on the musical traditions of the late Middle Ages and composed melodies for his own hymns. He was very pleased that the congregation could now join in and sing the chorales with the full conviction of their hearts. In Luther's view, music was an important tool for spreading the gospel: it was to be used to praise God, to comfort and encourage the faithful, and to teach people the true doctrine. The new order of worship was introduced to a mixed reception in the parishes. In the countryside, it was often opposed by the peasants, who remained attached to the old customs. Luther became increasingly impatient with their resistance and insisted that the new services be strictly enforced. The new order of worship was introduced in Wittenberg in 1525 and in the Electorate of Saxony in 1528. The Catholic Mass was replaced by the German Mass (Gottesdienst) and the Divine Service (Gottesdienst). The celebration of the Mass was replaced by the Lord's Supper (Abendmahl). The services were in German, and the congregation joined in with the prayers, psalms, and hymns. Luther's aim was to ensure that the gospel was preached and taught everywhere.

The rise of eSports, or electronic sports, has become a significant cultural phenomenon in recent years. What was once a niche hobby for video game enthusiasts has evolved into a global industry with a massive following and an enormous impact on popular culture. eSports refers to competitive video gaming, where professional players or teams compete against each other in various video games. The growth of eSports has been fueled by advances in technology, the widespread availability of high-speed internet, and the increasing popularity of video games as a form of entertainment. This essay will explore the rise of eSports and its cultural significance, including its impact on the gaming industry, its influence on popular culture, and its role in shaping the future of sports and entertainment.

The rise of eSports can be attributed to several key factors. Firstly, the advancements in technology have played a crucial role in the growth of eSports. The development of high-performance gaming hardware, such as powerful gaming PCs and gaming consoles, has enabled players to compete in video games with increasingly realistic graphics and immersive gameplay experiences. Additionally, the widespread availability of high-speed internet has made it easier for players to connect with each other and compete in online multiplayer games, laying the foundation for the growth of competitive gaming. Furthermore, the rise of streaming platforms such as Twitch and YouTube Gaming has provided a platform for professional players to showcase their skills and connect with their fans, further popularizing eSports as a form of entertainment.

The increasing popularity of video games as a form of entertainment has also contributed to the rise of eSports. Video games have become a mainstream form of entertainment, appealing to a wide audience across different age groups and demographics. As a result, the player base for popular video games has grown exponentially, creating a larger pool of potential competitors and fans for eSports events. Games such as League of Legends, Dota 2, and Counter-Strike: Global Offensive have become household names in the gaming community, attracting millions of players and viewers from around the world.

The cultural significance of eSports is evident in its impact on the gaming industry. The growth of eSports has led to the development of a professional gaming industry, with dedicated leagues, tournaments, and organizations that provide a platform for players to compete at a professional level. These organizations offer substantial prize pools, sponsorships, and endorsements, allowing professional players to make a career out of competitive gaming. The rise of eSports has also led to the creation of specialized gaming arenas and venues, where fans can gather to watch live eSports events, further legitimizing competitive gaming as a mainstream form of entertainment.

Furthermore, the rise of eSports has had a significant influence on popular culture. Professional eSports players have become celebrities in their own right, with dedicated fan bases and social media followings. The popularity of eSports events has led to mainstream media coverage and sponsorship deals with major brands, further integrating competitive gaming into popular culture. Additionally, the rise of eSports has sparked the development of eSports-related content, such as documentaries, podcasts, and news coverage, further cementing its place in popular culture.

The cultural significance of eSports extends beyond its impact on the gaming industry and popular culture. eSports has also played a role in shaping the future of sports and entertainment. Traditional sports organizations and entertainment companies have taken notice of the growing popularity of eSports and have made significant investments in the industry. Major sports leagues such as the NBA and NFL have established their own eSports leagues, while entertainment companies have begun to produce eSports-related content for television and online streaming platforms. This convergence of traditional sports and eSports has led to new opportunities for collaboration and cross-promotion, further blurring the line between traditional sports and competitive gaming.

In conclusion, the rise of eSports has become a significant cultural phenomenon with far-reaching implications. Its impact on the gaming industry, popular culture, and the future of sports and entertainment cannot be understated. As technology continues to advance and the popularity of video games grows, the influence of eSports is likely to continue to expand, further solidifying its place in popular culture. Whether you are a casual gamer, a dedicated eSports fan, or a traditional sports enthusiast, it is clear that eSports has become an integral part of our cultural landscape.

Online Hospitality Business: Establish and Conduct Business Relationships Report

Introduction

Online Hospitality business relates to the sale and purchase of legal hospitality products that can be purchased online by customers through Internet shopping. Customers can view details of the products they want to buy and then place an order. They would have to make payment through credit or debit card and once the payment is realised, the seller would despatch the products to the customer through courier. This model has been very effectively used by Amazon, eBay and other online companies and goods worth millions are sold every day. This paper provides a discussion of the business plan for setting up an online hospitality centre.

Business Relationships

Business relationships refer to the relationships that are built with the business partners to conduct and promote the business and in online shopping as well as conventional brick and mortar companies, this is very important. Business relationships help the company to sustain itself and grow. It helps to develop new opportunities, new collaborations, new strategies, new ideas and to sell new products. In the context of the online hospitality, the following trading partners are important (Leading Insight. 2005).

Manufacturer of the products

This is the one of the most important entity with whom a relationship of trust has to be developed. The online business cannot take up manufacture of all the items on their own and would need to source the products from the product manufacturers. This would begin with first deciding what hospitality products would be sold. Hospitality products can include glass fittings, furniture fittings, door controls, wall hangings, decorative items, personal hygiene products, wardrobe fittings, access control systems, architectural hardware fittings, wood connectors, sliding fittings, kitchen fittings used by hotels, hotel industries and even homes (Tylock, 2007).

The first step is to identify the manufacturers of such products. Yellow pages from any industrial area and even the Internet would give possible names and contact details of the manufacturers. These parties can be contacted through email, through telephone and through personal visits. It is very important that suitable agreements be reached with these manufacturers as to the quality, product type, delivery time, credit terms and a firm commitment on the price. This relationship can be developed by mutual trust since the manufacturer would be asked to deliver the products directly to the customer or to the online shopping site owner who would then repack the products after inspection and then despatch the products to the buyer. The relationship with the manufacturer can be made transparent by placing regular orders and making the payment promptly (Leading Insight. 2005).

Buyers

The buyer is the next important entity and the one who gives business. Relationship can be maintained by understanding the exact needs, making prompt deliveries of the right quality and quantity of products and taking back the products in case of any defects or other issues (Leading Insight. 2005).

Making the Business Successful

A variety of marketing tools would be used to make the marketing successful. Some of the methods that would be used are Blogs, Podcasting, Viral Marketing and Online Media. Blogs can be maintained that would give valuable insight into the current trends in the hospitality, features versus utility, prices, new products that add value, discussion of what other people are using and why and so son. The blog would be the best way for a marketing person to display the skill and expertise and the knowledge that one has. A list of potential bulk buyers can be obtained from the website of hospitality associations and these can be filtered as per the amount of business, the class of business, the reach, geographic location and so on. While mass mailers would help to reach a wider customer base, it would not be very effective since many of the recipients would label the mail as Spam and a tailored mail could not be effective. So there would be three or four different types of mailers, each directed for a different customer type. The owner of the online shopping should visit online conferences, physical tradeshows and network to get noticed so that the website gets noticed. In addition, the company should use the services of online marketing companies so that the company name would appear in the search engine list (Teten, 2005).

It is important that search engine optimisation – SEO should be used so that content and information about the site and the products would appear in the search engine when buyers would enter the keyword for searching products. This is a very important innovation and would help in bringing customers to the site. In addition, there should also be attempts to place small, unobtrusive advertisements in WebPages and other Internet sites, besides obtaining a listing in Internet sites such as Thomas Global, Ali Baba and others. Where possible, more and more information about the company, its products and the services along with the unique selling point should be highlighted. There are other models such as pay per click, but the efficacy of these methods is not clear and one never knows how much beneficial such methods have proved. Online lead generation method can also be used once the business is a few weeks old and starts appearing in the search engine rankings (Scott, 2007).

Business Report

The business report for the online hospitality is provided in this section (Teten, 2005).

Concept of the Business

The business model is a simple Internet-based online shopping model that has been widely used by a large number of Internet shopping sites. In this concept, we would have a B2B – Business to Business or a B2C – Business to Customer website that would have a number of items for sale. The concept of online shopping gallery would be used and information about the products would be displayed. Products would be arranged in the gallery as per different categories such as fittings, hygiene and beauty products and so on and it will be possible to search for a product using a search functionality. Visitors would be required to register and would be given a user name and password, free of cost. Very high 128-bit encryption would be used to provide maximum security. When visitors see the products they want, they can add it to the shopping cart and then pay for the purchase using credit card or cash on delivery. Once the payment is realised, the order would be processed and the order sent to the manufacturer for despatch as per the deadline. Payment would be done to the manufacturer once the goods are despatched to the customer. We can charge a small amount of commission for the sales from the customer and the manufacturer and this commission will be built into the price that is displayed on the screen. Courier charges would be extra and if it is in a nearby location, courier charges would below. The business would depend on volume and value on creating a good name (Teten, 2005).

Details of the plan

Details of the plan include (Teten, 2005):

  * Registering the domain name with the domain registering company and finding a hosting service that is prompt, provides sufficient web server space and has reasonable costs.
  * Setting up the website with all the functionalities. This can be done by outsourcing to website developers and the website would be hosted in a reliable hack-free web service hosting company.
  * Building a network of suppliers who would provide the required products. Product images would have to be taken along with rates, delivery time, etc.
  * Launching the site. It would be a good idea to hire some professional PR organisations who would take up the publicity campaign. Mailers, banner ads, content-based advertisements and other media would be used. Advertisement on TV and print media could be considered but this would be expensive.

Set Up Costs

Set up costs would have the following heads. The exact details would have to be worked out later (Teten, 2005):

  * Domain name registration and hosting charges.
  * Website development with outsourcing and an annual maintenance contract to maintain the website.
  * Expenses for PR and advertisement work.
  * Expenses for developing the manufacturer network.
  * Administration charges.
  * Salary and wages for self and staff who would process the orders.

  * Terms of contract : We herby enter into a contract that is mutually agreeable as per the following terms. Manufacturer FGH would undertake to supply following items as per the rates for xx days binding Product Name and Product Number: Quantity and Rate per piece:
  * Terms of delivery : Manufacturer would despatch the said products as per the destination given in the work order within the specified days. No extra surcharges are allowed. Based on the geographical location of the destination, ABC would reimburse the payment for courier charges.
  * Payment Terms : Within 2 weeks of the final delivery being made and after expiration of the terms of purchase by the buyer who can ask for a refund if the goods are not as per the order or deficient in any other respect.

Maximise Benefits for all parties

Investor would get his benefit he if the company performs well and his investment appreciates. This can be done by selling more products, increasing the value of the company. Manufacturer would get value when more of his products are sold and he gets prompt payment and increases his revenue. Staff and the owner would benefit when more and more products are sold and this would generate more revenue and enhance the brand (Teten, 2005).

Approval of Negotiations

Negotiations would have to be approved by clearly defining policies for purchase and payment terms and a firm commitment from the manufacturers. A benchmark would have to set that clearly outlines the requirements (Teten, 2005).

Feedback from Colleagues

The site would have a feedback page where visitors can give their feedback and suggestions for improvement. Valid suggestions would be evaluated for cost and practical considerations and implemented if found suitable (Teten, 2005).

Specialist Advice

Specialist advice would be required in the areas of PR and branding and in sourcing items from manufacturers (Teten, 2005).

Honouring Agreements

The contract letters have clearly defined terms and if these are met then it could be considered as honouring agreements. In case some items are not met, then the reason for not meeting the agreements would have to be analysed (Teten, 2005).

Adjustments to the process

Adjustments to the process would arise when delivery schedules are missed or when there is a mismatch between orders and deliveries or when one of the party fails to keep the commitment (Teten, 2005).

Nurturing Relationships

Nurturing relationships is very important for the success of the business. The investor would be informed through monthly progress reports about the state of the business, turnover achieved, number of new customers added, increase in value of the company and all other efforts to keep the investor informed. Manufacturers would be contacted through mailers and through telephone complimenting them on their performance and pointing out how they can improve (Teten, 2005).

The paper has examined important aspects of setting up an online hospitality business. Issues such as building business relationships, marketing and an extensive business report has been provided. The paper would hep those who are interested in developing such a business.
